messages:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding hit a weird edge with a HF model that requires trust_remote_code. conversion fails during tokenization step, stuck on special tokens. stack: 
```
ValueError: Special token id 50256 not in vocab
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/convert.py", line 214, in convert_tokenizer
```
maria: The model uses a custom config class + auto_map. huggingface's tokenizer has pad_token=None and some chat templates reference <|system|> which doesn't exist in token table. any quick ideas?
aj: Try converting with trust_remote_code=True and explicitly pass a special_tokens map. e.g. `python -m redwood.convert_hf --model org/custom-chat --trust-remote-code --special-tokens '{"pad_token":"<|pad|>","eos_token":"<|end|>"}'`
aj: Also verify `config.json` from the repo — custom config sometimes defines `bos_token_id` that doesn't match tokenizer.
samir: I saw this before — auto_map will lazy-load the custom class that mutates tokenizer in `__init__`. If you don't execute remote code, the tokenizer looks native and misses the injected specials. That's why trust_remote_code is needed.

maria: OK tried that, conversion progressed but now quantized runner crashes at generation with `kv_cache mismatch dimensions` after 2 tokens when using 4-bit quant. Works in fp16.
olivia: Quant + custom-attention kernels often assume fixed max_positions from config. Did the custom config change `n_ctx` or use relative pos enc?
maria: config.json has `n_positions: 8192` but the compiled kernels default to 2048. error trace: 
```
RuntimeError: KV cache size (2048) != expected (8192)
  at runtime/cuda/kernel.cu:451
```
aj: Short-term patch: force `config.n_positions=2048` in the converted config or rebuild kernels for the longer context. But note that changes to n_positions may alter model slicing/rotary embeddings. Run evals on a small prompt set after change.
samir: Also check chat template handling — the repo puts instruction wrappers in `chat_format.py` that assume `<|user|>` token exists and uses `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|user|>')`. If missing, the template ends up inserting raw string and breaks batching post-quant.
maria: Good catch. I grep for `<|user|>` and it's not in the vocab. I patched convert_hf to call `tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"additional_special_tokens": ["<|user|>","<|assistant|>","<|system|>"]})` before saving. That fixed template lookup but tests still show slight perplexity regression after 4-bit quant.
olivia: Perplexity changes after quant are expected. Try enabling smoother quantization config: `--qtype nf4 --qerr 1e-4` or run PQ chevalier script to fine-tune quant scales. Also enable prefix cache warmup when evaluating.

maria: After adding special tokens and forcing n_positions down, the model converts, passes unit gen test locally, but SLO infra job fails with a runtime mismatch on dedicated infra: `model signature mismatch: classifier_layer.weight shape differs`.

infra-bot: deploy-check failed on dedicated/gpu-pool-3. Logs archived at https://redwood.artifacts/1825012345

samir: That signature error smells like a different commit of model weights vs config.version. Did the HF repo use a sharded state dict or weight remapping in the custom class? Sometimes `from_pretrained` remaps keys.
aj: Check conversion log for `remapped_keys: {'lm_head.weight' -> 'output_head.weight'}` entry. If present, you need to apply the same remap during load into runtime.
maria: Found remap entries. Will re-run conversion with `--apply-remap`. Also adding an automated check that token ids for all special tokens exist post-convert.

olivia: Can you add a tiny eval run to CI that checks generation includes the right role tokens? e.g. prompt: `"<|system|>You are helpful.<|user|>Hi"` and assert decoder sees role ids.
maria: Yup adding that. thanks all :thumbsup:

aj: One more: file a short postmortem in eng-ml with steps: trust_remote_code note, special_tokens add, n_positions patch, remap flag. Make it a template for future HF bringups.
maria: Will do. Filing now.
